title: AI designed 16 working viruses that don't exist in any biosecurity database
description:
AI-designed viral genomes bypass biosecurity screening built only for known natural pathogens. Stanford and Arc Institute researchers used the Evo 2 genome model to design 16 complete bacteriophage genomes from scratch, and all 16 assembled into working viruses that killed their bacterial targets in the lab. Current DNA-synthesis screening relies on matching orders against databases of known organisms, a watchlist approach that fundamentally cannot flag a genome with no natural precedent to match against. The same generative capability that creates the blind spot also provides the repair: a model trained to predict what a genetic sequence will do can teach screening systems to evaluate function directly, replacing resemblance-based pattern matching with genuine biological comprehension. This research arrived under containment, published openly in Science, targeting bacteria with therapeutic potential against antibiotic resistance, so the governance conversation starts while the repair window is wide open.
